meta.title: AIKINGBOT — A team of AI agents working for you
meta.description: AIKINGBOT is a desktop app that runs a team of AI agents on your computer: many models, a skill Marketplace, schedules, voice and remote work through your own server. Free Windows Beta.
meta.docsDescription: Install AIKINGBOT on Windows, pair it with a server, update it and troubleshoot during the beta.

hero.title: A team of AI agents working for you, right on your computer
hero.lead: AIKINGBOT turns AI agents into a team: every bot has its own role, tools and schedule. Use Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok or your own model, install skills from the Marketplace and follow the work from any device through an AIKINGBOT server.
hero.note: Free during the beta · Windows 10/11 64-bit · Your data stays on your machine

features.title: Everything an AI team needs to do real work
features.lead: These capabilities ship in the beta. Items marked as needing setup require your own account or service.

team.title: AI agent teams
team.body: Create bots with their own roles and group them to work on one task together. Each bot keeps its own history, working folder and tools.

models.title: Many models and providers
models.body: AIKING Core with Claude, plus the Claude, ChatGPT/Codex, Gemini, Grok, Mistral, Groq, Cerebras and MiniMax engines and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint — local models included.

marketplace.title: Marketplace
marketplace.body: Install ready-made agents such as Media Producer, Ad Strategist, Trend Scout and Research Analyst, and skills for TikTok hooks, campaign briefs and meeting notes. Update or remove with one click.

skills.title: Skills and plugins (MCP)
skills.body: Extend bots with reviewed skills and MCP servers over stdio, HTTP or SSE. Tools with side effects always wait for your approval.

workspace.title: Workspace and files
workspace.body: Bots work in the folder you choose and read or create files, images and documents. Encrypted backup restores the whole workspace on a new machine.

schedule.title: Schedules
schedule.body: Run a bot once or on a schedule: a Monday morning report, a daily trend scan, a weekend inbox digest.

remote.title: Remote work
remote.body: Pair computers, browsers and phones with an AIKINGBOT server using one-time codes. Per-device permissions, revocable at any time.

voice.title: Voice calls with bots
voice.body: Talk to a bot directly: choose microphone and speaker, interrupt naturally, reconnect automatically. Requires speech-to-text and text-to-speech services you configure.

how.title: Four steps to a working bot team

download.title: Download
download.body: Get the Windows installer straight from the AIKINGBOT server and install it in a minute, no administrator rights needed.

connect.title: Connect
connect.body: Sign in with the AI plan you already use or add an API key. To work remotely, pair the app with an AIKINGBOT server.

team.title: Build your team
team.body: Pick agents from the Marketplace or create new bots, and give each one a model, skills and a working folder.

work.title: Delegate
work.body: Send a task, set a schedule or start a voice call. Follow progress, approve tools and get results right in the conversation.

download.title: AIKINGBOT for Windows
download.lead: Installers are served directly by the AIKINGBOT server, with a SHA-256 checksum so you can verify every file.

installSteps: Open the file. The beta is not code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen may warn you: choose "More info" → "Run anyway".
AIKINGBOT installs for your Windows account and opens. Follow the steps to pick an engine and sign in to a model.
To work remotely: Settings → Remote access, then paste the pairing link from your server.

items.a: The app is free during the beta. AI usage is billed by the model provider: use the ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or Grok plan you already have, a pay-as-you-go API key, or a free local model.

AIKING Core uses Claude through an Anthropic API key. The app also keeps the Claude, ChatGPT/Codex, Gemini, Grok, Mistral, Groq, Cerebras and MiniMax engines and OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Each bot can use a different model.

On your computer, in the .aikingbot folder of your Windows account. With an AIKINGBOT server, the remote workspace data lives on that server. Content is only sent to the model provider you choose for each conversation turn.
Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit, about 1 GB of free disk space and an Internet connection for cloud models. Linux builds (.deb, AppImage) exist too; macOS comes later.

items.q: What is the AIKINGBOT server for?
items.a: The server runs the same backend as the desktop app so bots keep working 24/7, lets you open the web app in a browser, pair several devices and share workspaces. The desktop app also works on its own without a server.

items.q: Can a bot run dangerous commands on its own?
items.a: No. Tools with side effects need your approval, and dangerous tools are refused unless you explicitly allow them. Remote devices pair with one-time codes, get scoped permissions and can be revoked. Voice never approves a tool.

The installer is not code-signed yet, so Windows warns on first install. The in-app interface is English for now; Vietnamese comes later. Voice calls need configured STT/TTS services. Composio OAuth connections need your own account. Back up important workspaces.
No. An update replaces the program only; data in .aikingbot is kept and migrated when needed. An older version refuses to open data written by a newer one to avoid corruption.

docs.title: Install, pair and update AIKINGBOT
docs.lead: A guide for the Windows Beta. The app interface is in English, so menu names are quoted as they appear.

sections.title: 1. Install on Windows
paras: Download AIKINGBOT-<version>-setup.exe from the Download section. Check its SHA-256 if you like (see Verify).
Open the installer. Because the beta is not code-signed, SmartScreen may show "Windows protected your PC": click "More info", then "Run anyway".
The installer needs no administrator rights, installs for the current account and creates an AIKINGBOT shortcut. The app opens when it finishes.
Portable (.zip): unzip into a folder and run AIKINGBOT.exe. The portable build does not update itself.

sections.title: 2. Connect a model
paras: On first start, choose an engine: AIKING Core (needs an Anthropic API key in Settings → Connections) or another engine such as Claude, ChatGPT/Codex, Gemini or Grok, then sign in with your plan.
You can add several accounts and keys; each bot picks its own model in its settings.

sections.title: 3. Pair with an AIKINGBOT server
paras: The server administrator gets a one-time pairing code (printed in the server log at start-up, or created in Settings → Remote access on an already paired device).
Browser: open <app>/pair and enter the code, or open <app>/pair#code=<code> directly.
Desktop app: Settings → Remote access → add a server and paste the aikingbot://pair… invite link created by the server. Every device gets its own permissions and can be revoked.

sections.title: 4. Updates
paras: Installers with an update channel check 15 seconds after start-up and every hour. When a new version exists, the app downloads it in the background, shows progress and a Restart button to install.
Manual check: Settings → About → Check for updates.
Data in %USERPROFILE%\.aikingbot (bots, conversations, skills, settings) is kept across updates.
0.3.0-rc.1 has no default update channel: install the newer installer over it once, and later versions update themselves.

sections.title: 5. Verify downloads
paras: Compare the result with the SHA-256 on the Download section or the SHA256SUMS file in the release folder.

sections.title: 6. Troubleshooting
paras: The app does not open: collect the logs in %APPDATA%\AIKINGBOT\logs and attach them to your report.
An update fails: download the latest installer from the Download section and install it over the current one; your data is not affected.
Pairing fails: pairing codes are single use and expire; create a new one and make sure you use the server's HTTPS address.
